What it runs

People call this a home lab. Usually it’s also a hobby.

The name makes it sound like one, and most of the time it is: config files, reverse proxies, a disk quietly filling up at 2am, an update that breaks everything the week you’re away. That’s the part that puts most people off, and it’s the part Sparky takes over. It installs what you ask for, wires it together, keeps it updated, backs it up, and restarts whatever falls over.

You ask it in Telegram, in plain English. “Set up Plex.” “What did I spend on the car last month?” It answers like an assistant would, except it can actually do the thing, because the machine is yours and it’s sitting in your hallway.

  • Your own film and TV library
  • Ad blocking across every device on your wifi
  • Home automation, with every smart device in one app instead of five, running on your box rather than through someone else’s cloud
  • Private file storage, with backups that happen nightly
  • Your expenses, your recipes and your bookmarks, kept on your machine instead of scattered across apps that read them

What comes with it

One box, one price.

  • The Sparky box, set up and ready to plug in

For a large film library you’ll want to add a hard drive. Sparky will tell you what it needs and set it up when you plug it in.

The included months start when your Sparky is set up, not when you order it. They are not a subscription — nothing renews, and we don’t take card details for them.
